html:
The Pipil are a Nahua people of western and central El Salvador, whose ancestors moved south from Mexico from around 900 CE. Their land was called Cuzcatlán.

They spoke Nawat, a language close to the Nahuatl of the Aztecs, and lived in towns of farmers who grew maize and cacao. When the Spanish came in 1524, the Pipil fought Pedro de Alvarado and wounded him, but were conquered within a few years.

Under colonial rule they lost much of their land to indigo and later coffee estates. The massacre of 1932 fell hardest on Pipil communities, and many hid their language and dress afterwards. Today only a few elderly people speak Nawat, and there are efforts to revive it in El Salvador.
sum: The Pipil are a Nahua people of western and central El Salvador, whose ancestors moved south from Mexico from around 900 CE. Their land was called Cuzcatlán.
